cmimc-2026-tcs-01a.prompt:
**Setting ("Calculators Made In Mellon College").** Every day, customers bring orders $(d_i,q_i,p_i)$: $d_i=1$ or $d_i=-1$ indicates the direction of the order (the officers sell to, or buy from, the customer), $q_i\le1000$ is the quantity and $p_i\le200$ is the price per calculator. The officers must fill an order entirely or not at all, and want to end the day with no calculators in inventory. Given a list of $n$ tuples $(d_i,q_i,p_i)$, find a subset $S\subseteq[n]$ that maximizes $\sum_{i\in S}d_iq_ip_i$ subject to $\sum_{i\in S}d_iq_i=0$.

For example, for the eight orders $(-1,4,41)$, $(1,5,44)$, $(1,3,45)$, $(1,100,40)$, $(1,11,43)$, $(-1,95,48)$, $(-1,3,43)$, $(-1,12,38)$ the maximum is $79$.

Give an algorithm that solves the problem in time $O(n^2)$ (treating the bounds on $q_i$ and $p_i$ as constants), and explain why it is correct and why it runs in that time.
cmimc-2026-tcs-01a.answer: A dynamic program over the running quantity balance $b=\sum d_iq_i$, which lies in $[-1000n,1000n]$, runs in $O(1000\,n\cdot n)=O(n^2)$; the example evaluates to $79$.
cmimc-2026-tcs-01a.reviewNote: No official solution exists for the TCS round; the algorithm was written by us and tested against brute force.
